page: Microsoft Azure FX12mds_v2 is a compute-optimized and memory-intensive virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a base clock of 4.2 GHz, configured with 6 physical cores and 12 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and an expansive 260 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), alongside cryptographic accelerators such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The platform features 252.0 GB of system memory, delivering 21.0 GB per vCPU, along with 944 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. There are no discrete GPUs allocated to this instance.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-core compute performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2,358.0 and text processing score of 2,953.0. Single-threaded throughput is also elevated in gzip compression at 34.76 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.36 GB/sec, each placing in the upper quartile. Small model LLM text generation reaches 398.8 tokens/sec, placing it in the top decile. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics remain within the median range due to the 12-vCPU cap, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,881.0, multi-core stress-ng at 13,325.9, and a PassMark CPU score of 22,880.91.

The primary tradeoff of the FX12mds_v2 involves its high memory-to-core ratio and strong single-core clock frequencies weighed against total multi-threaded execution scale. The 21.0 GB of RAM per vCPU is exceptionally high for a compute-focused line, and the 944 GB local NVMe SSD offers low-latency scratch space. This profile serves applications constrained by per-core licensing, single-thread clock speed, and high working-set RAM requirements, such as electronic design automation (EDA), in-memory analytics, relational database engines, and software compilation pipelines.
